notes:
Spec asserts: the real session runs ONE uninterrupted working span across the whole retry loop — the failing bash `false`, the corrective `echo recovered`, and the terminal reply — settling to ready exactly once at the end, never entering waiting. `waiting` is reachable only via permission_requested and the driver launches with --allow-all, so it is structurally unreachable.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-03: the real session is born directly into `working`, not `ready`. Copilot writes events.jsonl only when the first prompt is sent, so at discovery the file already holds the open turn, and since commit 3cde4f8d buildNewSessionState classifies that birth against its own metrics instead of hard-coding StateReady. The transient proc-<PID> row still carries the ready birth and is still the presession_birth anchor; session_birth and turn_start are now one phase.

KNOWN_FAILING (recording 2026-08-03-12-43-26, 4/5): copilot closes a turn after every tool call and opens the continuation ~80 ms later. This transcript has assistant.turn_end(turn 0) at 10:44:14.149Z, assistant.turn_start(turn 1) at 10:44:14.228Z, and turn 1's assistant.message only 7.2 s later at 10:44:21.476Z. parser.go maps assistant.turn_end to turn_done (→ ready) but lets assistant.turn_start fall to the default Skip arm, whose comment justifies it as "the open bracket of a turn the user message already put into working" — true for the first turn, false for a continuation turn, which has no preceding user.message. The daemon settled to `ready` at 12:44:16.383 while the model was still generating, and recovered only at 12:44:21.624 via "force ready→working on first activity": a 5.24 SECOND false `ready` in the middle of the retry loop, before the correct final settle at 12:44:25.497. This is the same defect as the sibling cell 2.2 auto-executed-tool-call, which showed it at 122 ms because the tailer happened to lag; here the tail kept up and the true magnitude is visible. The phases below assert the CORRECT behaviour and turn_end's invariant is what fails.

CORRECTION to the assessment: copilot does NOT report a non-zero exit as a failed tool call. `false` produced tool.execution_complete with data.success TRUE; the non-zero exit shows up only in data.result.content ("completed with exit code 1") and data.toolTelemetry.properties.shell_error_category ("command_nonzero_exit"). So the parser's IsError path is never reached by a shell failure, and the "data.success:false → IsError" reasoning in the assess body does not apply. The state consequence is unchanged — a tool completion must not settle the turn either way, and it did not.

The intermediate_working phase matches the same working transition as turn_start (the validator anchors at-or-after) and locks the narrow claim that the FAILED TOOL RESULT itself does not flicker the state — which held. The premature ready came from the turn boundary, not from the failure, and that is what turn_end's "no state_transition to working" invariant pins: a rebound proves the earlier settle was premature.

OBSERVATIONS: cost/tokens are asserted non-zero and are derivable from the staged transcript offline (assistant.message.outputTokens is copilot's live token signal; gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4-5 are both priced in the committed replay capacity snapshot). model is deliberately unpinned — --model accepts only `auto` and the router resolves gpt-5-mini or claude-haiku-4.5 per session.
